findings.statement: With the real SkellyCam stack, 5 cameras at 1080p60 do NOT sustain 60 fps when the MJPEG decode runs inside retrieve() on the capture loop: 44-47 fps per camera, with about 25% of sensor frames never grabbed. With a decode-free retrieve (memcpy) the same stack sustains 59.95-59.99 fps. 5x720p sustains 60 fps in both modes. Which bound applies to a real DSHOW camera is open: it depends on where DSHOW decodes MJPEG.

Lockstep gate: https://github.com/freemocap/skellycam/blob/23ccbf208e43879bfc74fc01049e5af2a623933d/skellycam/core/camera_group/camera_orchestrator.py#L96-L109

findings.statement: No grabbed frame was lost on the way to disk in any run. Recorded frame numbers were consecutive, every MP4 decoded to exactly the recorded count, and RecordingFinalizer validation passed. The losses happen before the recorder: frames the sensor produced that the lockstep loop never grabbed. SkellyCam's frame_number and finalizer statistics cannot see them (the finalizer reports 'Mean Framerate 44.52 Hz' with no gap). So priority 1 currently holds only for grabbed frames.
findings.evidence: e_e2e_*.json fields per_camera.consecutive, files[].decoded_frames, sensor_frames_never_grabbed, stop_error=null, finalizer_stats; c_record.json all_frames_on_disk=True. Code: https://github.com/freemocap/skellycam/blob/23ccbf208e43879bfc74fc01049e5af2a623933d/skellycam/core/camera/opencv/opencv_helpers/opencv_get_frame.py#L79 (frame_number counts retrieves)

findings.statement: At 1080p mjpeg the serial per-iteration work in each camera process exceeds the 16.7 ms budget: retrieve about 11-12 ms under load (6.98 ms isolated), plus put_frame about 4.1 ms, plus record_frame about 1.3 ms. The group interval rises to a 21-22 ms median, and the slowest camera sets the rate for all cameras.

put_frame makes 2 full-record copies per frame: copy.copy (6,221,432 B at 1080p, allocated on the heap every frame) and then the slot assignment (6,221,432 B). That is 3.73 GB/s at 5x1080p60, 1.87 GB/s of it avoidable. Isolated, production put_frame costs 1.35 ms at 1080p against 0.174 ms for one np.copyto into the same slot (7.8x). Under e2e load it costs 2.3-4.2 ms.
findings.evidence: f_copies.md 1080p record path rows; a_write.md rows 1080p 1 production vs single_copy_reference; e_e2e_summary.md put_frame column. Code: https://github.com/freemocap/skellycam/blob/23ccbf208e43879bfc74fc01049e5af2a623933d/skellycam/core/ipc/shared_memory/ring_buffer_shared_memory.py#L118-L133

findings.statement: The ring write path itself is not the throughput limit: even with 5 unthrottled writers, put_frame sustains 337 fps per camera at 1080p (819 at 720p). But production put_frame only reaches about 10.6-11.5 GB/s aggregate, where a single copy reaches 38-50 GB/s.

The default record path (writer_fourcc X264, resolved to MSMF H.264) keeps up with 5x1080p60 when paced: 60.0 fps per camera, record_frame p99 5.2 ms, max 9.3 ms, no write over 16.7 ms, no frames missing from the files. But it costs about 11.7 logical CPUs (1169% summed process CPU; about 2.3 CPUs per camera). write() is asynchronous: release takes 1.8-6.5 s after unthrottled runs. Derived encode throughput is about 116 fps per camera at 5x1080p.

findings.statement: The UI path cannot reach 60 fps at 5x1080p. With no browser and an instant ack, get_latest_multiframe + create_frontend_payload costs 10.9 ms median (p99 23.8) per payload on the event-loop thread, giving 43.7 payloads/s; the FreeMoCap by-number path costs 15.4 ms (37.9/s). In the full e2e run the UI reached 34.8-41.0 payloads/s at 1080p and 55-60 at 720p. Turning the UI off did not raise capture fps (46.1 without UI vs 44.0/46.8 with), so in these runs the UI is not what limits capture.

findings.statement: Every measured copy matches the verified frame_copies list: copy.copy + slot assignment in put_data, a view handoff to the encoder, rotate only when rotation is set, the 632 B metadata copy, the UI np.copyto x N, resize, rotate-before-resize, the JPEG tobytes/assemble/slice copies, and the get_images_by_frame_number allocation. findings.statement: type_overloads.py L23 crashes spawned children whenever a SkellyCam ring DTO is unpickled before any multiprocessing.Queue (AttributeError: module 'multiprocessing' has no attribute 'queues', exit code 1). The crash depends on argument order, which extends W30.

Existing diagnostics: check_shm_speed.py is stale (ImportError at line 8). test_shared_memory.py now passes with the normal conftest (21 passed), because polars 1.43.0 is installed in the SkellyCam venv now (W28's ModuleNotFoundError no longer reproduces). Combined with the orchestrator and payload tests: 58 passed, 1 known failure (test_video_file_path_from_config).

With memcpy capture, cross-camera grab spread under lockstep is small: p99 0.84-1.22 ms. With mjpeg at 1080p it is p99 3.6-4.8 ms. Sensor tick to frame written: about 5 ms median at 1080p memcpy, 26-27 ms median (p99 about 39 ms) at 1080p mjpeg.
findings.evidence: e_e2e_summary.md columns 'cross-cam grab spread p99' and 'sensor tick -> written'

limitations: The machine was not idle: other sessions' research jobs (USB camera, MJPEG, GigE and UDP benchmarks) ran throughout; system CPU just before runs was 11-64% (env blocks in each JSON). p99/max values and 720p read rows are noisy. The 1080p mjpeg e2e result was reproduced in 3 runs (44.0, 46.8, 46.1 fps).

No real cameras were used. Two DSHOW devices (indices 0, 1) were detected, but other jobs held them under a camera lock. The e2e capture is a FakeCapture with assumed buffer-size-1 'latest frame wins' semantics. Whether DSHOW decodes MJPEG inside retrieve() (mjpeg mode) or elsewhere (closer to memcpy mode) is an open question; the two modes bracket it. The mjpeg stand-in adds one memcpy, and its q90 synthetic JPEGs (540 KB at 1080p) may differ from a real camera's MJPEG.

Encode cost and file sizes depend on the synthetic content (gradient + moving box + ±8 noise). Whether MSMF H.264 runs on the GPU or in software was not established; the about 2.3 CPUs per 1080p60 camera suggests software (inference).
Unthrottled record encode throughputs are derived (frames / (loop time + release time)), not measured directly, because write() is asynchronous on MSMF.

Copy counting (bench_f) is single-process with in-process wrappers. The JPEG tobytes, assemble and slice copy sizes are analytic. Copies inside DSHOW, MSMF, the H.264 encoder and the websocket stack could not be counted.
The UI benchmarks have no browser: the ack is instant and there is no websocket send, so the UI rates are upper bounds on the server side; permessage-deflate and send costs are not included.

bench_f_copies.py and the first bench_e_e2e.py run hung at interpreter exit after writing all results (stopped by timeout, exit 124); both scripts now call os._exit(0). The workaround import of multiprocessing.queues is present in all scripts (needed because of the type_overloads.py bug).

Large temporary files: the e2e recordings (1.0-2.3 GB per run) and the bench_c files were deleted by the scripts after their sizes were recorded. The bench_f leftovers (about 20.8 MB, sizes in results/bench_tmp_leftover_sizes_before_delete.txt) were deleted manually. Empty subfolders remain in the scratch bench_tmp folder because the safety check blocked removing directories by glob. SkellyCam's own TRACE log file was written to its default log path.
